en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest eagles in the world.
The Philippine Congress is the legislative branch of government, consisting of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over two thousand years ago for agriculture.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white flower scientifically known as Jasminum sambac, is the official national flower of the Philippines.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator for newborns and was the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a dance of two steps forward and one step backward.
Baybayin is an ancient precolonial Philippine writing system where each character represents a syllable rather than a single letter.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is a complex volcano featuring a main crater lake on Volcano Island within Lake Taal.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, citizens who are at least eighteen years old have the right to vote in elections.
Fernando Amorsolo was the first National Artist of the Philippines, famous for painting rural landscapes with backlighting techniques.
